categories.otherDefinition: 'Other businesses' = Animal Nutrition Division (AND, mainly DL-methionine sold back-to-back on high-seas basis) + Environmental Health Division (EHD: household/public-health insecticides). Bio-rationals/biostimulants sit inside PGR and other categories, not a separate line.
keyBrands: Yunico / Yunico Flow (chlorantraniliprole, made at Tarapur)
Excalia Max / Indiflin (SCC patented paddy fungicide, launched FY26)
Lentigo (imazosulfuron, SCC rice herbicide, launched FY26)

parent.name: Sumitomo Chemical Company, Limited (SCC), Japan
parent.parentScale: SCC agro division revenue ~USD 3.02 bn (CY/FY24), ~4% of global crop-protection market, 8th largest globally; among top-3 by patents issued 2007-24
parent.scilWeightInParent: SCIL ~12% of SCC group PAT in FY25 and ~45-50% of SCC's market cap (Anand Rathi estimate)
parent.businessModel: SCIL has exclusive right to distribute SCC-innovated molecules in India under SCC brand/trademark; buys technical from SCC in many cases and formulates locally. Also distributes Valent BioSciences (US subsidiary) bio-rationals and Sumitomo Biorational Co products (Topgrain). Sells SCC-innovated products manufactured in India back to SCC (custom synthesis/CSM).
parent.royalty: Historically no royalty paid (none in last 3 years). From FY27: 3% of net sales on 2 (possibly more later) SCC products for which SCIL may now buy technical from third parties; approval cap Rs 2 cr; management says actual will be lower and margin-accretive. SCC does not charge royalty to other group companies because they must buy technical from SCC.
parent.csmSalesToParent: Rs 100-150 cr p.a. (Rs 110-140 cr expected FY27); to grow from FY28-29 as Dahej/Tarapur projects commission

relatedPartyFY27Approved_RsCr.note: AN purchase estimate assumes Rs 500/kg vs FY26 reference price Rs 200-211/kg on 8,740 tonnes (price spike after Middle-East conflict). Transactions expected to cross LODR materiality for first time; ordinary resolution at 27-Jul-2026 AGM.

parent.animalNutrition: Distribution of SCC animal-nutrition products (methionine) in India discontinued in FY26 on SCC global realignment (Q3FY26 revenue hit ~Rs 72 cr), then restarted from ~May 2026 because of global supply disruption. Back-to-back high-seas sales with fixed margin of ~4-5%, no price/inventory/FX risk to SCIL.
parent.exportsToParent: Japan exports Rs 136.6 cr in FY26 (Rs 119.8 cr FY25). In H1FY27 exports to Japan roughly halved because of over-stocking at the parent; management expects normalisation next year. ~25% of exports go to group companies, ~75% to third parties (Oct-2024 call).
parent.newMoleculeAccess: India elevated by SCC to the same tier as Japan, Brazil, North America and Europe for early-stage trials of SCC discovery molecules; 2 molecules received for Indian trials ahead of global launch (May-2026 call). 3-4 SCC molecules in pipeline, of which Excalia Max launched.
parent.manufacturingHubRole: SCC said it intends to use India as a manufacturing hub; capex at Dahej/Tarapur/Bhavnagar is for SCC global supply. ICICI Securities (Apr-2026) cites management that anticipated order size for SCC products over 3-4 years is ~USD 1.5 bn.
parent.semiconductor: SCC's ICT & Mobility division plans commercialisation of high-purity semiconductor chemicals in India; SCIL management said meetings with government/customers were held jointly. On 19-Sep-2026 SCC (parent) signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to explore semiconductor materials supply incl. a possible chemicals plant in India; SCIL is not named and its role is undefined (Oct-2026 call: 'at MoU stage'). Separate July-2026 parent news: SCC's Korean unit Dongwoo Fine-Chem JV with Samsung Electro-Mechanics (outside India).
parent.restructuringOrDelisting: No announcement of delisting, open offer, OFS or merger with other group entities found in 2024-26. SCC has held exactly 75% (MPS cap) since FY21 OFS.
nomineeDirectors: Tadashi Katayama (President, Agro & Life Sciences sector, SCC)

pipeline.patentedVsGeneric: Generic 71-72% / specialty 28-29% of revenue (FY26/H1FY27); specialty ~30% of domestic revenue
pipeline.biologicals: Bio-rationals/biostimulants ~8-10% of revenue vs industry <5% (mgmt); sales of bio products were blocked roughly Jun-Dec 2025 pending approvals under new biostimulant regulations; approvals received Nov-Dec 2025

capex.policy: Invest ~15% of consolidated EBITDA annually in upgrades/expansion (deck); further Dahej projects of similar size (~Rs 150 cr each) to be announced roughly one per year; I-Sec cites Rs 250-300 cr every two years at Dahej

guidance.formal: No formal revenue/EPS guidance (company policy, reiterated 27-Oct-2026)
guidance.margin: Aim to keep EBITDA margin at or above 20%; 'stable' performance incl. margins expected (Oct-2026)
guidance.h2fy27: Challenging: extended El Nino, reservoirs ~71% of capacity, uneven rain, possible lower rice acreage; wheat expected normal; focus states UP, Chhattisgarh, AP, Karnataka, TN; grapes/wheat/cumin look better
guidance.exports: Japan (parent) shortfall seen as a one-year phenomenon; normal next year
guidance.growthAspiration: I-Sec (Apr-2026) quotes management targeting 12-14% revenue CAGR over next 3-4 years (not repeated in 2026 calls); CRISIL expects 7-10% medium-term growth and 19-20% operating margin
guidance.pricing: Price hikes 15-Mar, 1-Apr, 1-May 2026 (cost inflation 10-25% by product); prices corrected from June as costs eased
guidance.cashUse: No plan to return surplus cash now; evaluating strategic acquisitions; board may return unused cash in future
guidance.transformation: 'Good to Great' programme (people, operations, technology, data/digital, collaboration); financial targets to be shared later

workingCapital.definition: Company NWC = inventory + receivables - payables - other financial liabilities (the last is mostly dealer scheme/discount accruals and deposits); days on COGS (inventory, payables) or revenue (receivables, OFL) for the period
workingCapital.comment: FY26 NWC rose to 103 days (89) on deliberate pre-kharif stocking and shorter payables; receivable days improved to 83 (91). Sep-26 inventory days 115 (95) on price increases and soft liquidation; corrective action in H2FY27. CRISIL expects inventory to rise to 110-120 days; company imports 50-55% of raw materials.

accounting.rebatesAndDiscounts: Revenue is net of rebates/discounts: FY26 Rs 333.1 cr = 9.3% of gross contracted revenue (FY25 9.6%, FY24 10.5%, FY23 10.2%, FY22 12.3%, FY21 11.7%). Auditor flags accrual estimation as a key audit matter.
accounting.schemeLiability: 'Liabilities for additional discount and scheme' Rs 335.9 cr at Mar-26 vs Rs 288.3 cr at Mar-25 (+16.5% vs revenue +3%); total other current financial liabilities Rs 454.7 cr (Mar-26) and Rs 566.5 cr (Sep-26). Company treats them as working-capital offsets.
accounting.salesReturns: Rs 22.4 cr in FY26 vs Rs 9.0 cr FY25, Rs 46.5 cr FY24, Rs 50.0 cr FY23 (0.6% of gross in FY26); management says no sales-return policy and no herbicide returns in FY26

exceptionalItems.item: Past-service cost from new Labour Codes (consolidated Rs 16.11 cr; standalone Rs 15.19 cr)
Business-interruption insurance claim for FY23 Bhavnagar fire

accounting.otherIncome: Treasury income is large: FY26 other income Rs 146.7 cr = ~20% of PBT; MarketsMojo computes non-operating income at ~44% of a recent quarter's profit. Screener's Q1FY27 other income (Rs 74 cr) includes the Rs 26.9 cr exceptional item.
accounting.animalNutritionPassThrough: High-seas animal-nutrition sales (Rs 184.8 cr FY26; Rs 265.0 cr FY25) are back-to-back at ~4-5% margin; FY27 approval assumes Rs 1,000 cr purchases at higher methionine prices - can inflate revenue and depress margin %
accounting.goodwill: Barrix goodwill Rs 60.4 cr; Barrix FY26 PAT Rs 0.08 cr (FY25 Rs 6.3 cr) - impairment is a key audit matter
accounting.consolidation: Two subsidiaries reviewed as immaterial; one reportable segment
accounting.fx: Exports and imports roughly equal at USD 70-80 mn each a year; exposure hedged

notes: Distribution: 15,000+ distributors, ~40,000 dealers, 60 depots, 26 states, ~600 sales staff, 1,500+ contractual field officers, 4.4 mn farmers met physically; CRISIL says distribution covers ~85% of India.
Employees 1,622 at 31-Mar-2026. R&D: 3 DSIR-approved labs, 75+ scientists; R&D spend Rs 14.4 cr = 0.45% of turnover in FY26.
Seasonality: H1 (kharif) was 58% of FY25 and 61% of FY26 revenue (derived from deck: H1 1,827/3,149 and 1,987/3,238); company says business is best judged annually.
Domestic growth has been weak: management concedes peers grew faster; standalone domestic sales Rs 2,607 cr FY23 -> Rs 2,485 cr FY26.
Screener's reported FY25 dividend payout of 80% is a period mis-allocation: the Rs 5 special dividend belongs to FY24.
